Rashi on Sukkah 52a:10:1.hebrew: פניו אל הים הקדמוני - המקדש הראשון, שהוא כים, שהיו הכל נקבצים שם — כים שכל הנחלים הולכים אליו:
Rashi on Sukkah 52a:10:1.english: Its face toward the eastern sea - The First Temple, which is like the sea, as everyone would gather there, like the sea into which all the streams flow.

Rashi on Sukkah 52a:10:2.hebrew: ועלה באשו וצחנתו - ומפני שהעלה באשה וסרחון, שהניח האומות ונתגרה בישראל:
Rashi on Sukkah 52a:10:2.english: “And its foulness shall rise, and its stench” - And because it brought up foulness and stench, [in] that it left the nations [alone] and incited against Israel.

Rashi on Sukkah 52a:11:1.hebrew: נקדים וניזיל באורחא - נשכים בהשכמה קודם היום. השכמה קרי קדמותא בש"ס:
Rashi on Sukkah 52a:11:1.english: Let us rise early and go on the road - Let us rise early, before day[break]. Rising early is called *kadmuta* in the Shas.

Rashi on Sukkah 52a:11:2.hebrew: כי הוו פרשי מהדדי - שהיו משתי עיירות והגיעו לפרשת דרכים, פירש זה לכאן וזו לכאן:
Rashi on Sukkah 52a:11:2.english: When they were taking leave of each other - For they were from two [different] towns, and [when] they reached a crossroads, this one went this way and that one [went] that way.

Rashi on Sukkah 52a:11:3.hebrew: אורחא רחיקא - דרך רחוקה היא בין שתי מקומותינו, ואי אפשינו עוד לילך יחד:
Rashi on Sukkah 52a:11:3.english: A long way - It is a long distance between our two places, and we do not wish to walk together any further.

Rashi on Sukkah 52a:11:4.hebrew: וצוותין בסימא - אילו היינו יכולים לילך בדרך אחד, היה נעים צוות שלנו:
Rashi on Sukkah 52a:11:4.english: And our company is pleasant - Had we been able to walk along one path, our company would be pleasant.

Rashi on Sukkah 52a:12:1.hebrew: אי מאן דסני לי - אם היה שונאי מתייחד עם האשה, לא הוה מצי אוקומי אנפשיה מלחטוא. ועל עצמו היה אומר:
Rashi on Sukkah 52a:12:1.english: If [it were] one who hates me - If my enemy had been secluded with the woman, he would not have been able to restrain himself from sinning; and he was speaking about himself.

Rashi on Sukkah 52a:12:2.hebrew: תלא נפשיה - נשען על בריח הדלת, כאדם שמחשב ומצטער:
Rashi on Sukkah 52a:12:2.english: He suspended himself - He leaned against the bolt of the door, like a person who is pondering and distressed.

Rashi on Sukkah 52a:1:1.hebrew: וספדה הארץ - בנבואת זכריה, ומתנבא לעתיד שיספדו על משיח בן יוסף שנהרג במלחמת גוג ומגוג. וכתיב: ״משפחת בית דוד לבד ונשיהם לבד״ — שאפי' בשעת הצער צריך להבדיל אנשים מנשים:
Rashi on Sukkah 52a:1:1.english: And the land will eulogize - [This is] in the prophecy of Zechariah, and he prophesies about the future that they will eulogize Messiah son of Joseph who was killed in the war of Gog and Magog. And it is written: “The family of the house of David separately, and their women separately” — [showing] that even at a time of grief, it is necessary to separate men from women.

Rashi on Sukkah 52a:1:2.hebrew: שעסוקין בהספד - באותה שעה, והמצטער אינו מיקל ראשו מהר. ועוד, שאין יצר הרע שולט — כדקאמר קרא: ״והסירותי את לב האבן״, ולקמן אמר שהקב"ה שוחטו — כו' אמרה תורה כו':
Rashi on Sukkah 52a:1:2.english: When they are involved in a eulogy - At that time; and one who is in distress does not readily act with levity. And furthermore, [the Gemara states] that the evil inclination does not dominate [them] — as Scripture states: “And I will remove the heart of stone” (Ezekiel 36:26), and later [the Gemara] says that the Holy One, Blessed be He, slaughters it — etc., [and yet] the Torah said, etc.

Rashi on Sukkah 52a:1:3.hebrew: כאן שעסוקין בשמחה - וקרובה לקלות ראש, ועוד שיצה"ר שולט עכשיו — לא כל שכן:
Rashi on Sukkah 52a:1:3.english: Here, when they are engaged in rejoicing - And [joy] is close to levity, and furthermore the evil inclination dominates now — is it not all the more so?

Rashi on Sukkah 52a:3:1.english: And they shall look unto Me because they have thrust him through - They will look at the slain one before them.

Rashi on Sukkah 52a:3:2.english: And they shall mourn for him, as one mourns for an only son - Like a person who eulogizes an only son that he had, and who died.

Rashi on Sukkah 52a:4:1.english: The righteous weep - For they recall the distress they had in overcoming this evil [inclination] during their lifetimes.

Rashi on Sukkah 52a:4:2.hebrew: כי יפלא בעיני וגו' - סיפיה דקרא: ״גם בעיני יפלא״:
Rashi on Sukkah 52a:4:2.english: “If it be wondrous in the eyes of,” etc. - The end of the verse [states]: “It should also be wondrous in My eyes.”

Rashi on Sukkah 52a:5:1.english: Of a bukhya - [A] spider, which they call iraigne.

Rashi on Sukkah 52a:5:2.hebrew: ולבסוף - משאדם נמשך אחריו מעט, מתגבר והולך בו:
Rashi on Sukkah 52a:5:2.english: And ultimately - Once a person is drawn after it a little, it grows progressively stronger within him.

Rashi on Sukkah 52a:5:3.hebrew: מושכי העון בחבלי השוא - בתחלה היו מביאין אותו עליהם ע"י חבלים שאינן של כלום:
Rashi on Sukkah 52a:5:3.english: Those who draw iniquity with cords of vanity - Initially, they would bring it upon themselves by means of cords that are of no substance.

Rashi on Sukkah 52a:5:4.english: And like a wagon rope - A thick rope with which they tie the cow to the plow.

Rashi on Sukkah 52a:6:1.english: I will tell of the decree - I will recount this matter to be a decree and a memorial.

Rashi on Sukkah 52a:6:2.english: This day have I begotten you - Today I will reveal to people that you are My son.

Rashi on Sukkah 52a:8:1.english: If your enemy is hungry - Your evil inclination is hungry and lusts for sin.

Rashi on Sukkah 52a:8:2.hebrew: האכילהו לחם - הטריחהו במלחמתה של תורה, דכתיב: ״לכו לחמו בלחמי״ (משלי ט׳:ה׳):
Rashi on Sukkah 52a:8:2.english: Give him bread to eat - Make him toil in the battle of Torah, as it is written: “Come, eat of my bread” (Proverbs 9:5).

Rashi on Sukkah 52a:8:3.hebrew: השקהו מים - תורה, דכתיב בה: ״הוי כל צמא לכו למים״ (ישעיהו נ״ה:א׳):
Rashi on Sukkah 52a:8:3.english: Give him water to drink - [This refers to] Torah, as it is written concerning it: “Ho, everyone who thirsts, come to the water” (Isaiah 55:1).

Rashi on Sukkah 52a:8:4.hebrew: ישלימנו לך - שיהא שלם יצרך עמך ואוהבך, ואל ישיאך לחטוא וליאבד מן העולם:
Rashi on Sukkah 52a:8:4.english: Will reconcile it to you - That your [evil] inclination will be at peace with you and love you, and will not entice you to sin and perish from the world.

Rashi on Sukkah 52a:9:1.hebrew: הצפוני - כדמפרש, צפון בלבו של אדם:
Rashi on Sukkah 52a:9:1.english: The northern one - As [the Gemara] explains, [it is] hidden in the heart of man.
